name: Codex CLI
hook_surface_note: Executable native Codex Stop transport for the canonical EXEC-RESPONSE-01 gate (T-1551): the hook forwards the Stop event's `last_assistant_message` to `tools/saipen.py response check --classify` -- the SAME renderer/checker OpenCode's text gate uses -- and maps the verdict onto Codex hook output. No response schema lives in the adapter. The Stop gate enforces by requiring a correction continuation; it never retracts rendered text. Re-entry is bounded deliberately: the first invalid stop of a turn requests exactly one correction, and a stop that is already a Stop-hook continuation (`stop_hook_active`) records the exact capability boundary CODEX_STOP_REENTRY_NO_FAIL_CLOSED instead of looping. Trust is an external host boundary: Codex skips non-managed hooks until the operator reviews and trusts the hash-bound definition via /hooks, and installing never marks a hook trusted. CODEX_STOP_TEXT_CLASSIFICATION: the Stop event carries no turn ingress or tool context, so a markerless reply on an idle turn is indistinguishable from ordinary chat and passes.
response_enforcement_note: The supported Stop event supplies the outgoing final message and one correction continuation is enforced. SEPARATE EVIDENCE, not part of this claim: the hook requires host trust, and a Stop that is already a continuation records CODEX_STOP_REENTRY_NO_FAIL_CLOSED rather than closing fail-closed. POST-RENDER: text already exists and may already be visible; no retraction or hard invisible prevention. Each fresh Stop gets the same canonical gate; re-entry remains one correction, not fail-closed.
admission_enforcement_note: UNAVAILABLE: the shipped Codex transport is a Stop hook only. It has no delivery hook and no pre-output boundary, so it cannot observe that authority reached the model and cannot stop a reply before it exists. The admission layer is reported NOT_ENFORCEABLE for this host, never passed as admitted.
execution_capability_note: EXECUTION.md instructs silent tool continuation. No supported pre-render intermediate-text interception is installed; final/Stop hooks cannot retract streamed text. Machine progress uses canonical status and runtime heartbeat. Native thought UI is host-owned. Higher-priority host narration requirements take precedence and prevent a silence guarantee.

name: ZAICODE
home_note: ZAICODE runs with an isolated HOME (<workspace>/.zaicode/home) and never shares ~/.zcode with a production ZCode; ZAICODE_HOME names that HOME, and an unset variable means ZAICODE is not configured on this machine.
hook_surface_note: ZAICODE loads this process hook from ~/.zcode/cli/config.json and runs it as argv with shell:false, which is why the installer writes it with HOOK_BOOTSTRAP and the broker's max_shells:0 policy. The SKILL and instruction surfaces stay inside ZAICODE_HOME (the isolated home); the hook config is the operator profile's ~/.zcode because that is the file the running host reads. Without this declaration the canonical injector skipped the hook step entirely and runtime_bootstrap.hook_problems answered [] at any drift, so a repaired artifact never reached the operator (T-1934/T-1935).
